clue.text: Capital site developed — most comely!

indicators.note: a site that is developed is rebuilt into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Bonn was the capital of West Germany in 1984
the word site, rearranged

explanation.surface: A capital city's building site has been developed into something most attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: Bonn was West Germany's capital when this ran in 1984.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonny is a Scottish and northern word for pretty, so its superlative means most attractive.

clue.text: See Oriental agent

parts.note: E for east, the Orient
a secret agent

explanation.surface: An instruction to go and see an agent from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, a slightly literary verb for spotting something.

clue.text: Inlets flowing to join up

indicators.note: flowing water moves and mixes, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of the word, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Small bays and creeks flow together and merge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Join up' suggests streams meeting, but it means signing up for the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist is to enrol in the army or navy, which is what joining up means.

clue.text: Dissatisfied camera man's order: "To horse!"

parts.note: surface reading: a cavalry command to mount up
setter's reading: a film-maker unhappy with a take orders it filmed again

explanation.walkthrough: The horse is also in the pun: said aloud, the answer sounds like a farrier being told to shoe it again.
explanation.definitionFit: A cameraman unhappy with footage calls for the scene to be filmed once more.

clue.text: Nearly fall in for an antiseptic

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the final letter of the phrase is dropped

parts.note: the parade-ground order to fall in means form a line

explanation.surface: A soldier nearly falls in on parade while carrying an antiseptic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall in' is the drill command for soldiers to form a line; drop its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Formalin, a solution of formaldehyde in water, is used as a disinfectant and preservative.

clue.text: Captain of the brass?

parts.note: surface reading: the leader of a brass band or of top military officers
setter's reading: a famous fictional naval captain whose name describes a player of a brass instrument

explanation.walkthrough: C. S. Forester's Captain Horatio Hornblower is the naval hero; his surname splits into horn blower, a brass player.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional Royal Navy captain's surname literally describes someone who plays a horn.

clue.text: Citric acid dispenser?

parts.note: the letters of the word, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Something that dispenses the citric acid found in lemons.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no separate anagram signal; the question mark flags that 'Citric' is to be rearranged and 'acid dispenser' is a playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A harsh reviewer is known for biting, sour remarks, so handing out acid is the job.

clue.text: Fiddlesticks! — It's in no way associated with logic

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an exclamation dismissing something as rubbish

definitions.text: It's in no way associated with logic
definitions.meaning: second meaning: read as ..., the thing that lacks all sense

explanation.walkthrough: The second half splits the word into NON and SENSE: something with no connection to sense or reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiddlesticks is an old exclamation meaning rubbish or twaddle, just as the answer is.

clue.text: Given off by uranium indoors, experimentally

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, the things given off

indicators.note: an experiment tries things in new arrangements, so the combined letters are shuffled

parts.note: read as in doors: the element's symbol goes inside the word doors
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A lab note warning that uranium kept indoors gives off something during an experiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indoors' must be split as 'in doors': U goes inside DOORS and the result is rearranged. The definition is loose, since odours are what is given off.
explanation.definitionFit: Smells are emitted or released by things, so the clue's phrase stands loosely for that noun.

clue.text: Made from 80 per cent nylon, just

indicators.note: something made from material reshapes it, so the kept letters are rearranged
eighty per cent of a five-letter word keeps four letters and drops the last

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A clothing label claiming a fabric is made from just eighty per cent nylon.
explanation.walkthrough: Four-fifths of NYLON is NYLO, which is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and the answer are synonyms meaning merely or no more than.

clue.text: Emptiness without' activity. — it's cruelty

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: inanity is emptiness or vacuity
a hum of activity: busy movement

explanation.surface: A moralist complains that empty idleness, a life with nothing doing, amounts to cruelty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but in its older sense it means outside, so the first word wraps around the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhumanity is brutal, merciless behaviour, a direct synonym for cruelty.

clue.text: Tree in the wrong setting for overhead protection

indicators.note: in places the tree's name inside the setting that surrounds it
wrong signals letters out of their proper order, to be rearranged

parts.note: an elm is a tree
the word the, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A gardener notices a tree planted in the wrong setting, where it would shelter overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: ELM sits inside a jumbled THE; 'setting' reads like part of the picture but just links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A helmet is head armour, protection worn over the top of the head.

clue.text: Maternity wear?

parts.note: surface reading: clothes for pregnant women
setter's reading: a garment for the head worn by a mum, and the state of being a parent

explanation.walkthrough: Split it as MOTHER HOOD: a hood a mother might wear, which is also the state of being a mother.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the state of being a mother, the same idea as maternity.

clue.text: It could make a duck sick, ill, out of sorts

definitions.text: It could make a duck sick, ill, out of sorts

indicators.note: out of sorts here means not in proper order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, shaped like O
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spill at sea that would leave a duck sick, ill and out of sorts.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, and within it duck (O), sick and ill are rearranged; a duck is a zero score in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Spilled petroleum coats waterbirds' feathers and poisons them, so an oil spill really does sicken ducks.

clue.text: Law takes lead in representation

indicators.note: in puts the single letter inside the word for a likeness

parts.note: a statue is a sculpted representation of someone

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its front, so only its opening letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter of takes

explanation.surface: A legal maxim: the law takes the lead in how things are represented.
explanation.walkthrough: The T heading 'takes' goes inside STATUE, between its second T and U.
explanation.definitionFit: A statute is a written law passed by a legislature, so it is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Not cured — beaten!

parts.note: the letters of both words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient left uncured is a beaten one.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no separate anagram signal; 'beaten' serves as both definition and hint that the letters are knocked about.
explanation.definitionFit: To be trounced is to be soundly defeated, a strong synonym for beaten.

clue.text: Where letters may be seen briefly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: letters of the alphabet are found inside a word
second meaning: to put it shortly

explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' suggests the post, but they are letters of the alphabet, which appear within any word.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for summing something up concisely, the same as briefly; read literally it locates letters.

clue.text: Persuasive speech delivered by Eric Roth

indicators.note: a speech delivered is reworked into its spoken form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of the name, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man named Eric Roth gives a convincing address.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhetoric is the art of persuasive speaking or the language it produces.

clue.text: Part of school charge

parts.note: surface reading: a division of a school, such as the junior or senior part
setter's reading: such a division is what a teacher is put in charge of

explanation.walkthrough: The parse is uncertain: 'charge' may be read as the group of pupils placed in a teacher's care.
explanation.definitionFit: A school is divided into sections, each a distinct part with its own staff.

clue.text: In which a letter may be seen to hide another letter

definitions.text: In which a letter may be seen

parts.note: to envelop is to wrap up and conceal
a letter of the alphabet, chosen to fit

explanation.surface: A riddle about mail: a letter inside something that hides yet another letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'letter' is a posted one; the second is a letter of the alphabet. 'Another letter' leaves which one open, so the crossings settle it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail travels sealed inside this paper wrapper, which keeps the posted letter out of sight.

clue.text: Approached artist (Turner?) in want

indicators.note: in puts the painter's letters inside the word for lack

parts.note: want and need both mean lack
RA, Royal Academician; J. M. W. Turner was one

explanation.surface: A struggling painter, perhaps Turner, was approached while poor.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of London's Royal Academy of Arts, as the painter Turner was.
explanation.definitionFit: To have neared somewhere is to have come close to it, as approached means.

clue.text: Exchange rate adjusted in transport system

indicators.note: something adjusted is altered, so the letters are rearranged
in puts the rearranged letters inside the abbreviation for the railway

parts.note: BR is British Rail, Britain's old national railway
the word rate, rearranged

explanation.surface: The exchange rate is adjusted to suit a transport network's finances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exchange rate' looks like one phrase; 'Exchange' is the definition. BR was British Rail, the UK state railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Barter is trading goods directly for other goods, a form of exchange without money.

clue.text: Sounds like a number of players disqualified

indicators.note: sounds like says the answer is heard as another word when spoken

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians

explanation.surface: Several players in a team have been disqualified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' suggests a sports team, but they are musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone banned is barred from taking part, which is what disqualified means.

clue.text: Saw nothing amiss in a capital

indicators.note: amiss means wrong or out of place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of both words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A visitor to a capital city reports seeing nothing wrong there.
explanation.definitionFit: Washington DC is the seat of the United States government, its national capital city.

clue.text: Blow back and forth

indicators.note: a word that reads the same back and forth is one that reads identically either way

parts.note: to blow a horn or whistle briefly

explanation.surface: A short instruction to blow back and forth, like a wind or a breath.
explanation.definitionFit: To toot is to blow a horn or whistle, a sense of the verb blow.

clue.text: Kind girl may do it in the pool

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sort or category

definitions.text: girl may do it in the pool
definitions.meaning: second meaning: what an office worker does at a keyboard in a typing pool

explanation.walkthrough: The pool is not for swimming: a typing pool was an office's shared group of typists.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means a kind or sort, and the verb is what a typist does on a typewriter.

clue.text: About to change position in class

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to move is to change position

explanation.surface: A pupil is about to change seats in the classroom.
explanation.walkthrough: In some British public schools the Remove is the name of a particular form, or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a form in certain English schools, an uncommon sense of class meaning year group.

clue.text: Excessively reimbursed — though proved roughly about first-class

indicators.note: roughly means approximately, so the letters are only loosely in order
about means surrounding, so the shuffled word goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: the word proved, rearranged
A1 means first-class, written with the letter I for the digit 1

explanation.surface: Someone was reimbursed too generously, though it was roughly proved their work was first-class.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-class) is used as AI, a standard crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: To be paid more than is due is to be given too much money in return.
